extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of the PARI/GP system (mathematicians and programmers using the PARI library or gp interpreter)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP functions: describes semantics, return types, special cases, examples, library-call signatures, and cautions for using each function in gp and in the library API.

rubrics_metrics.name: Str({x}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts its argument list into a single character string (type t_STR, the empty string if x is omitted). Arguments are evaluated in string context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To recover an ordinary GEN from a string, apply eval. Mostly useless in library mode; in library code prefer strtoGEN/GENtostr to convert between GEN and char*. GENtostr returns a malloced string that must be freed after usage. Example: Str(x, i) -> "x2"; eval(%) -> 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strchr(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts x to a string, translating each integer into a character (ASCII).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works on integers and vectors of character codes. Examples: Strchr(97) -> "a"; Vecsmall("hello world") gives vector of ASCII codes and Strchr on that vector returns the original string. Library syntax: GEN Strchr(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strexpand({x}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concatenates arguments into a single string and then performs environment variable expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to read environment variable values. Arguments read in string context. Example: Strexpand("$HOME/doc") -> "/home/pari/doc".

rubrics_metrics.name: Strtex({x}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Translates its arguments to TeX format and concatenates them into a single string (type t_STR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments are read in string context. Produces TeX-formatted representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vec(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms object x into a row vector; optional parameter n specifies dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n omitted or 0, default depends on x's type: vectors/quadratic forms return as row vectors; polynomials/power series return coefficient vectors (polynomial: starting with leading coefficient; power series: significant coefficients in increasing degree); matrix returns vector of columns; string returns vector of characters; map returns domain vector; t_ERROR returns error components. For matrix/string/map/error, n is meaningless and must be omitted. If n provided and nonzero, zeros appended/prepended to reach |n|. Vec is reciprocal of Pol/Ser in respective contexts. Library syntax: GEN gtovec0(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vecrev(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent to Vec(x, -n) then reverse the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly: reciprocal of Polrev (vector coefficients start with constant term then increasing degree). Library syntaxes: GEN gtovecrev0(GEN x, long n) and GEN gtovecrev(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vecsmall(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like Vec(x, n) but returns a vector of type t_VECSMALL; only works when result representable as vector of small integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x is a string, returns vector of ASCII codes (Strchr yields back the string). Library syntax: GEN gtovecsmall0(GEN x, long n) and GEN gtovecsmall(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: binary(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs vector of binary digits of |x|. For reals, returns integer-part and fractional-part digit vectors; for vectors/matrices, applies per-component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By convention 0 has no digits (binary(0) -> []). Examples: binary(10) -> [1,0,1,0]. Library syntax: GEN binaire(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: bitand(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise AND of two integers x and y; negative numbers handled 2-adically (limit of bitand on sequences tending to x and y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is ordinary integer, possibly negative. Examples: bitand(5,3)=1; bitand(-5,3)=3; bitand(-5,-3)=-7. Library API: GEN gbitand(GEN x, GEN y). Also GEN ibitand(GEN x, GEN y) returns bitwise and of |x| and |y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitneg(x, {n = -1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise negation of integer x truncated to n bits (n>=0); special n=-1 means no truncation (infinite leading 1s represented as negative number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined as summation over bits not(xi)2^i up to n-1. Negative-argument behavior follows 2-adic rules as in bitand. Library syntax: GEN gbitneg(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: bitnegimply(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise 'negated imply' (not (x ⇒ y)) of two integers x and y, computed per bit: (xi andnot(yi))2^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative-argument behavior as for bitand. Library syntax: GEN gbitnegimply(GEN x, GEN y). Also GEN ibitnegimply(GEN x, GEN y) for |x|,|y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitor(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise inclusive OR of two integers x and y (per-bit xi or yi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative-argument behavior handled 2-adically. Library syntax: GEN gbitor(GEN x, GEN y). Also GEN ibitor(GEN x, GEN y) for |x| and |y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitprecision(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Without n: returns floating-point precision in bits of PARI object x (exact objects return +oo). With positive n: creates new object equal to x with requested bit-precision (rounded up to machine word multiples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For vectors/matrices: operation is componentwise; for series/polynomials: coefficientwise. For real x, n is number of desired significant bits; if n smaller than current precision, x truncated; otherwise extended with zeros. Exact or non-floating types unchanged. Examples given. Library syntax: GEN bitprecision0(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: bittest(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns nth bit of x starting from right (coefficient of 2^n) as 0 or 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 3.2.20 for negative-argument handling. Library syntax: GEN gbittest(GEN x, long n). For t_INT x, low-level variants exist (long bittest(GEN x, long n) and ulong int_bit(GEN x, long n) for n >= 0). Examples: bittest(7,0)=1; bittest(7,3)=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitxor(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise exclusive OR (XOR) of integers x and y, per-bit (xi xor yi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative-argument behavior as in bitand. Library syntax: GEN gbitxor(GEN x, GEN y). Also GEN ibitxor(GEN x, GEN y) for |x|,|y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: ceil(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceiling function: smallest integer >= x for real x; for rational functions returns Euclidean quotient numerator/denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gceil(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: centerlift(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like lift but t_INTMOD and t_PADIC components are lifted using centered residues: for Mod(.,n) gives y with -n/2 < y <= n/2; for p-adics uses centered residue modulo p-adic precision if valuation non-negative; otherwise returns fraction with pv centerlift(...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alias centerlift(x,'v) allowed for backward compatibility. Use bestappr for rational reconstruction. Library syntax: centerlift(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: characteristic(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the characteristic of the base ring over which x is defined (from t_INTMOD and t_FFELT components); raises exception on incompatible primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: characteristic(Mod(1,24)*x + Mod(1,18)*y) -> 6. Library syntax: GEN characteristic(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: component(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracts the nth component of x according to PARI internal layout (components counted after initial code words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreted per type: vectors -> nth element; matrices -> nth column; polynomials -> nth coefficient (degree n-1); power series -> nth significant coefficient. Prefer polcoeff for polynomials and [] operator for vectors/matrices. Use requires detailed knowledge of internal type layout and thus should almost never be used; exceptions exist (e.g., p-adic accuracy stored as component). Library syntax: GEN compo(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: conj(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate of x; for real quadratic numbers means conjugation in the quadratic field. No effect on integers, reals, intmods, fractions, or p-adics. polmod is forbidden (use conjvec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gconj(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: conjvec(z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate vector representation: if z is polmod Mod(a,T), returns vector of length deg(T) containing embeddings/conjugates, or for finite fields the Frobenius conjugates; integers/rationals return themselves; vectors return matrix of conjugate vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If T has rational coefficients returns complex embeddings via polroots(T); if T has intmod coefficients returns conjugates accordingly. Library syntax: GEN conjvec(GEN z, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: denominator(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominator of x: for rational numbers/functions clear; integers/polynomials treated as rationals with denominator 1. For recursive structures, returns lcm of denominators of components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For polynomials prefer denominator(content(x)). t_INTMOD and t_PADIC have denominator 1; t_POLMOD denominator is that of minimal-degree polynomial representative. Warning about multivariate objects created according to variable priorities with possibly surprising effects. Library syntax: GEN denom(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: digits(x, {b = 10})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns vector of digits of |x| in base b (default 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By convention 0 has no digits (digits(0) -> []). Examples: digits(123) -> [1,2,3]; digits(10,2) -> [1,0,1,0]. Library syntax: GEN digits(GEN x, GEN b = NULL). Use fromdigits to invert.

rubrics_metrics.name: floor(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Floor function: largest integer <= x for real x; for rational function returns Euclidean quotient numerator/denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gfloor(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: frac(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fractional part of x, identical to x - floor(x). For real x, result in [0,1[.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gfrac(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: fromdigits(x, {b = 10})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives integer formed by elements of x seen as digits in base b (inverse of digits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By convention empty list yields 0. Examples: fromdigits([1,4,4,1,4],5) -> 1234; fromdigits([]) -> 0. Library syntax: GEN fromdigits(GEN x, GEN b = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: hammingweight(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is t_INT, returns binary Hamming weight of |x|; otherwise for pol, vec, col, vecsmall, mat returns number of non-zero coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: hammingweight(15)=4; hammingweight(x^100 + 2*x + 1)=3; for identity matrix returns number of ones on diagonal. Library syntax: long hammingweight(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: imag(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaginary part of x. For quadratic numbers, returns coefficient of ω in canonical integral basis (1, ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gimag(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: length(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of x; #x is shortcut. Returns number of components appropriate to type: vectors -> dimension, lists -> number of entries, matrices -> number of columns, strings -> number of characters (excluding trailing \0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined for arbitrary GP types but awkward elsewhere (e.g., integers have two codewords so length returns effective length minus 2). Examples shown. Library syntax: long glength(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: lift(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Lifts components: if v omitted, lifts intmods from Z/nZ to Z, p-adics from Qp to Q (truncate), and polmods to polynomials; otherwise lifts only polmods whose modulus main variable is v. t_FFELT and List elements are not lifted (convert List to vector or use apply(lift,L)). Components where lift meaningless are copied verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lifts performed recursively but only one level: once a t_POLMOD is lifted its components are not further lifted. Use liftall to lift recursively as long as possible, liftint to lift only intmods/p-adics, liftpol to lift only polmods, centerlift for centered residues. Library syntax: GEN lift0(GEN x, long v = -1) and GEN lift(GEN x). Examples show subtle interactions with variable priorities and Mod objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: liftall(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift all components of x from Z/nZ to Z, from Qp to Q (truncate), and polmods to polynomials; t_FFELT and List elements not lifted (convert or use apply(liftall,L)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies components where lift meaningless. Examples show usage. Library syntax: GEN liftall(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: liftint(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift only t_INTMOD components from Z/nZ to Z and Qp to Q (truncate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: t_FFELT and List elements not lifted; convert lists or use apply(liftint,L). Library syntax: GEN liftint(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: liftpol(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift only t_POLMOD components to polynomials; other types copied verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: t_FFELT and Lists not lifted; use apply(liftpol,L) for lists. Example usage and library syntax: GEN liftpol(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: norm(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic norm: product of x with its conjugate(s). For vectors/matrices taken componentwise (not Euclidean L2 norm). Norm of a real element is its square to be compatible with complex norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gnorm(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numerator(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator of x: for rationals/functions obvious; integer or polynomial treated as rational with numerator x. In other cases numerator(x) = denominator(x) * x; for recursive structures lcm of denominators used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For polynomials prefer numerator(content(x)). t_PADIC and t_INTMOD have denominator 1 so numerator is itself. Warning about multivariate variable priority effects. Library syntax: GEN numer(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numtoperm(n, k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generates k-th permutation (row vector length n) of numbers 1..n using lexicographic ordering starting at 0; k taken modulo n!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse of permtonum. Library syntax: GEN numtoperm(long n, GEN k).

rubrics_metrics.name: oo
rubrics_metrics.description: Represents +∞ (and -oo for -∞); comparable to real numbers with expected ordering: +∞ greater than any real number, -∞ smaller than any real number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in functions such as intnum. Library syntax: GEN mkoo().

rubrics_metrics.name: padicprec(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns absolute p-adic precision of x: minimum precision of components; returns +oo for exact objects. Raises exception on incompatible objects or incorrect types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided showing exception messages. Library syntax: GEN gppadicprec(GEN x, GEN p). Also long padicprec(GEN x, GEN p) returning LONG_MAX if x=0 and the p-adic precision as a long integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: permtonum(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a permutation x on n elements, returns number k such that x = numtoperm(n,k) using standard lexicographic numbering starting at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse of numtoperm. Library syntax: GEN permtonum(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: precision(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Without n: returns precision in decimal digits of x (exact objects return +oo). With n: creates new object equal to x with new floating point precision n (number of significant decimal digits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For t_REAL components, n smaller truncates, larger extends with zeros. For exact/non-floating types no change. Also notes about different available functions (GEN precision0, GEN gprec, long precision) and that in those forms accuracy is expressed in machine words. Examples show behavior. Library syntax: GEN precision0(GEN x, long n); also GEN gprec and long precision(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: random({N = 2^31})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a random element in various natural sets depending on argument N: integer in [0,N-1], real in [0,1) with same accuracy as N, intmod random, ffelt random, for vec length-2 returns integer in [a,b], for elliptic-curve objects returns a k-rational affine point (not uniformly distributed), for polynomials returns random polynomial of degree at most degree(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses a single internal generator (Brent's XORGEN). getrand returns seed, setrand resets generator; same seed yields same sequence. Not suitable for cryptographic purposes. Library syntax: GEN genrand(GEN N = NULL). Also GEN ellrandom(GEN E) and GEN ffrandom(GEN a). Examples demonstrate behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: real(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns real part of x; for quadratic numbers returns coefficient of 1 in canonical integral basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN greal(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: round(x, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Rounds real x to nearest integer (ties to +∞) and sets e to number of error bits (binary exponent of difference between original and rounded value).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operates on every coefficient at every level of a PARI object (unlike other truncation functions). Example demonstrates rounding of polynomial coefficients differently from truncate. Use to obtain exact results after approximate computation when theory indicates integer coefficients. Library syntax: GEN round0(GEN x, GEN *e = NULL); GEN grndtoi and GEN ground also available.

rubrics_metrics.name: serprec(x, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns absolute precision of x with respect to power series variable v; minimum precision of components; +oo if x exact as series in v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises exceptions for incompatible types. Examples show usage. Library syntax: GEN gpserprec(GEN x, long v) and long serprec(GEN x, GEN p) returning LONG_MAX if x=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplifies x as much as possible: e.g., complex/quadratic number whose imaginary part is integer 0 converted to real part; polynomial degree 0 converted to constant term; simplifications occur recursively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful before arithmetic functions which expect integer arguments. GP results are simplified before stored in history unless automatic simplification disabled. Library syntax: GEN simplify(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sizebyte(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs total number of bytes occupied by the tree representing the PARI object x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long gsizebyte(GEN x). Also long gsizeword(GEN x) returns words count.

rubrics_metrics.name: sizedigit(x) [DEPRECATED]
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated: outputs a quick upper bound for number of decimal digits of components of x (off by at most 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t use. To count decimal digits of a positive integer use #digits(x). To estimate size recursively use normlp(x). Library syntax: long sizedigit(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: truncate(x, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Truncates x and sets e to number of error bits. For real x, chops off fractional part; e is binary exponent of difference (fractional part). For rational functions returns Euclidean quotient and e is not set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exponent of x too large compared to precision (e>0) result undefined and error occurs if e not given. Applies componentwise to vectors/matrices (e is maximal error bits). Special use: applied to power series transforms it into polynomial/rational function by chopping O(X^k); for p-adics transforms into integer/rational by chopping O(p^k). Library syntax: GEN trunc0(GEN x, GEN *e = NULL); also GEN gtrunc and GEN gcvtoi variants exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: valuation(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes highest exponent of p dividing x; semantics depend on type of p (integer or polynomial) and type of x (integer, intmod, fraction, q-adic, polynomial, power series, vector, complex/quadratic), returns minimum of component valuations for composite types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x = 0 returns +oo for exact objects. For p-adic numbers or power series returns exponent of zero. Raises error for wrong type combinations. Library syntax: GEN gpvaluation(GEN x, GEN p) and long gvaluation(GEN x, GEN p) returning LONG_MAX if x=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: varhigher(name, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a variable name whose priority is higher than priority of v (or of all existing variables if v omitted); counterpart to varlower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display name is arbitrary string used only for printing; not usable to retrieve variable. Creating many such variables consumes limited variable slots — don't create unless necessary. Use varhigher("tmp", x) carefully to avoid exhausting variables. Library syntax: GEN varhigher(const char *name, long v = -1) where v is variable number. Examples demonstrate variable priority pitfalls and advice to request only needed priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: variable({x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives main variable of object x (variable with highest priority used in x); returns p if x is a p-adic number; returns 0 if no variable attached. If x omitted returns list of user variables known to interpreter sorted by decreasing priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to test whether variable attached: if (!variable(x),...). In library mode do not use for non-NULL x (gvar is more appropriate); for p-adics gel(x,2) gives p; long gvar(GEN x) returns variable number or NO_VARIABLE. Examples show interactions when varhigher/varlower used.

rubrics_metrics.name: variables({x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns list of all variables occurring in object x (or all user variables if x omitted), sorted by decreasing priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to test whether variable attached: if (!variables(x),...). If varhigher/varlower used, same display name may appear multiple times corresponding to different priorities. Library syntax: GEN variables_vec(GEN x = NULL); GEN variables_vecsmall(GEN x) returns sorted variable numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: varlower(name, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a variable name whose priority is lower than priority of v (or of all existing variables if v omitted); counterpart to varhigher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New GP variables created by interpreter normally have lower priority than existing ones; varlower can create variable with requested priority but consumes limited variable slots. Display name arbitrary and cannot be used to retrieve variable. Use carefully to avoid exhausting variables. Library syntax: GEN varlower(const char *name, long v = -1). Examples demonstrate session-history dependent failures and safe usage patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcendental functions: general precision/conversion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for evaluating transcendental functions (which always return inexact objects with finite precision): behavior depends on argument types (inexact real/complex, exact integer/rational/polmod, polmod).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rules: (1) If argument is real or inexact complex, computation done with argument's precision. (2) If argument is integer/rational/exact complex/quadratic, convert it to real/complex using current precision settings (defaults realprecision in decimal digits or realbitprecision in bits) before evaluation; change precision via \p, default(realprecision,...) or in bits via \pb or default(realbitprecision,...). (3) In library mode precision taken from function's prec parameter (prec >= 3), and prec not used when argument already inexact. Note that some accuracies available on 32-bit machines may not be attainable on 64-bit machines. (4) If argument is polmod (algebraic number), function is evaluated on each complex embedding; returns column vector with one component per embedding (degree of modulus). Examples show precision behavior (sin(Pi/4) with differing realprecision). See individual function help for branch cuts and principal value choices.
